progress.summary: TICKET-008 complete. All four DB-008 ticketing code-drift objects dispositioned individually from re-derived evidence: get_enhanced_artist_stats and ticket_notifications are dead consumers (deletion NOT performed, both out of grant); settlements and track_venue_profile_view are accepted debt with named decision owners. Two of the inventory's four file-level attributions were falsified. No product code changed; the deliverable is the recorded disposition plus an executable fence that makes a resurrection fail the suite.
completed: Re-homed HF-DB008-TYPECHECK-TICKETING from TICKET-006 to this task, and recorded in TICKET-006 that the type-drift cluster was not part of its scope and was not performed.

Corrected the task's scope.in, which named the wrong four objects. It listed ticket_sales.ticket_type, artist_financial_transactions.category and booking_requests.venue_id — those are the ARTIST cluster's settlement surfaces, not the ticketing cluster's. The authoritative set is the ticketing cluster's four: get_enhanced_artist_stats, settlements, ticket_notifications, track_venue_profile_view.

Built a schema-aware chain resolver and negative-controlled it. It resolves each unqualified CREATE to the FIRST existing search_path entry, which is what makes the absence claim correct: 20260821025543 sets search_path = private, public, so ticketing_migration_issues is a private-schema relation. My first resolver answered public and the fence caught it.
Proved all four objects are created in NO schema of the active chain (320 top-level files) and appear nowhere in lib/database.types.ts, so regeneration cannot fix any of them.

get_enhanced_artist_stats -> dead consumer. Zero code callers; the inventory's consumerVerdict 'live' with 4 liveConsumers is falsified. The one file the inventory filed under the ticketing domain, lib/marketplace/ticket-source-adapter.ts, has an empty rpc() surface entirely. Canonical capability: lib/public-artist/artist-stats.ts. Already fenced by two artist-lane tests.

ticket_notifications -> dead consumer. Re-validated zero use: one repository reference, the .from() at lib/services/ticketing.service.ts:343, inside sendTicketNotification, which occurs exactly once (its own definition). The module is LIVE via components/ticketing/ticket-purchase-form.tsx:14, so the inventory's 'unreachable module' verdict is wrong and only the method may be deleted. DELETION NOT PERFORMED (lib/services/** is design-system's grant). Corrected the TICKET-005 recipe: also delete getNotificationTitle (384-396) and getNotificationMessage (398-410), each of which occurs exactly twice and becomes dead with the method.

settlements -> accepted debt, NOT a dead consumer. Two live out-of-grant consumers remain (lib/venue/finance-snapshot.ts:112, app/api/admin/finances/settlements/route.ts:99), and the chain admits an out-of-band apply: 20260720021441 is marker-only (body `select 1;;`, no DDL token) and records the settlements tables as 'already applied via execute_sql'. The repository therefore holds both 'the chain never creates it' and 'some target has it'. The ticketing share is already closed by TICKET-005 (canonical = ticket_revenue_allocations + financial_transactions, absence reported as settlement: null / settlement_available: false); the object itself needs a target catalog read.

track_venue_profile_view -> accepted debt. Not dead: app/api/venues/[id]/route.ts:109 is an entry-reachable route, and no canonical replacement exists — the function AND its backing table venue_profile_views are both created in no schema. The ticketing attribution is false; the webhook route contains no occurrence. Already handed to venue by TICKET-005.

Recorded exec_sql as a prohibition: created in no schema, and its only repository SQL reference is a REVOKE in 20260717194541, which is evidence it must not exist. Fenced so creating it fails the suite.

New finding raised to venue: lib/venue/finance-snapshot.ts:117 folds the unreadable settlements read into a false zero (settlementsRes.data || [] -> settlement_status 'unsettled'), so a venue is told its revenue is unpaid when the truth is unavailable. The admin consumer of the same relation already fails closed with 503 finance_unavailable, so the handoff is venue-only.

Cross-checked against TICKET-005's three handoffs so no drift is dispositioned twice: HF-TICKET-035-TICKET-NOTIFICATIONS (design-system, still accepted/unapplied) and HF-TICKET-035-TRACK-VENUE-PROFILE-VIEW (venue, still accepted/undecided) remain the execution paths; HF-TICKET-035-ARTIST-STATS-RPC was informational and needs nothing. This task supplies the evidence, it does not duplicate the requests.

Wrote and mutation-proved the fence __tests__/ticketing/db008-drift-cluster-disposition.test.ts (44 tests). Three live mutations each failed the expected cases: restoring the dead settlements read fails 3, deleting settlement_available: false fails 1, and weakening queries() to a substring test fails 5. The settlements route was restored to a byte-identical SHA (a69c253f74b04a21c3b7a9e5cef7b36756ac2bbf) after each.

Confirmed TICKET-006's three columns are known-pending regeneration, not drift: issuance_slot, dedupe_key and issuance_alerted_at are authored in 20260927120000_ticketing_issuance_slot_dedup.sql and absent from lib/database.types.ts, because CP-051 forbids applying it here and the --linked target is permanently disqualified.
